name: PressBridge
summary: Self-hosted MCP server that lets Claude edit, update and repair WordPress sites over SSH, with backups, approval mode and a nightly security watch.
best_for: WordPress agencies and freelancers who look after several client sites on their own servers and want Claude to edit and update them with backups, an audit log and limits on what it can touch
skip_if: you are on shared hosting without SSH, you want a plugin you install from the WordPress dashboard, you need a vendor with a large team behind it, or you want a tool we have tested ourselves
honest_knock: It needs SSH and Docker or Python on a server you run, so shared hosting without SSH is out. The safety claims (backups, syntax checks, blocked commands) come from the vendor page and we have not tested them. Database changes such as plugin updates are not covered by its file backups. It is a small project from a single maker, so check support and update history yourself.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Solo · per one-time, Free $0 for 1 site read-only
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-15 on the PressBridge home page, US dollars) PressBridge is a self-hosted MCP server that lets Claude work on WordPress sites over SSH and WP-CLI. The Free edition costs $0 and covers 1 site, read-only. Solo costs $49 one time for one person and unlimited sites. Agency costs $100 one time for your whole team, with unlimited sites and servers, approval mode, WooCommerce tools, an audit log and three Claude skills. The page says Solo includes everything in Agency. Agent costs $15 a month after 14 days free and adds Watch, a nightly security check of every site with alerts. One-time licenses include a year of updates and email support and keep working after that. Every plan has a 14-day refund. Prices are in USD and taxes such as EU VAT are added at checkout by the reseller, which is the merchant of record. Watch can also ask Claude to review each alert, billed to you by Anthropic on your own API key. We have not paid for a plan.

compare_with.why: The vendor contrasts PressBridge with MCP plugins that run inside WordPress, which it says go down with the site. Compare how each handles a broken site, backups and approval before you pick.
